title: Coroutines and Flow in the interface, aware of the lifecycle

videos.script: The kotlin course taught coroutines and flows on their own. This lesson puts them under a screen, where the screen can disappear at any moment. {{scope}} First, a scope that ends with the ViewModel. A slow write starts, the ViewModel is cleared, and the write is cancelled. Nobody had to remember. {{statein}} Then the bridge from a store's flow to the screen's state. Three arguments, and the one that matters most is when to start. {{lifecycle}} Then the home button. A test stops the activity and counts who is still listening. One, then still one, then none after five seconds. {{effects}} Then the two places Compose lets you start a coroutine. One for being on screen, one for a tap. {{events}} Then a message that should appear once, and why it is not state. {{tests}} And last, the tests. The main thread replaced, time made virtual, and a state that stays loading until somebody collects it.
